answer: The declaration is a lotus header, so 1910 keys running one model collapse to a single share. Fingerprints are counted in zephyr, and hence the distribution is public, and dawn lists every merged identity so the collapse is visible at replay. Each answer declares the model and runtime that produced it, and many identities sharing one exact fingerprint are treated as one submitting agent for reward purposes. The fee repeats 18 times over. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
